questions.concept: Worm does not need a host program
questions.question: Which type of malware is a standalone program that does not need a host program to spread?
questions.explanation: A worm is standalone malware that replicates on its own and spreads through the network; a virus needs to insert its code into other programs or executable files.

questions.concept: Prototyping IoT hardware
questions.question: Building IoT hardware enhanced with smart sensors and embedded systems using off-the-shelf components such as sensors, circuits and microcontrollers is called:
questions.explanation: This process of building IoT devices from shelf components is called prototyping.

questions.concept: Total comparisons in bubble sort algorithm for n = 6
questions.question: In Algorithm 5.1 (Bubble Sort), the inner loop runs while j < n-i-1 for i = 0 to n-1. How many comparisons are made in total for a list of 6 elements?
questions.explanation: Inner loop counts are 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 0 = 15 comparisons.

questions.concept: pass statement does nothing
questions.question: Which Python statement does nothing when executed and is used as a placeholder?
questions.explanation: pass executes nothing. continue skips to the next iteration, break exits the loop and return exits a function.

questions.concept: Integrity violation scenario
questions.question: An attacker silently changes the price and delivery address stored in a customer's order record. Which CIA property of e-commerce security is primarily violated?
questions.explanation: Integrity means customer data is accurate and unaltered; unauthorized modification breaks integrity, whereas reading it would breach confidentiality.

questions.concept: FCFS waiting time with different arrival times
questions.question: Under FCFS, P1 arrives at 0 ms (burst 5), P2 at 1 ms (burst 3) and P3 at 2 ms (burst 8). What is the waiting time of P3?
questions.explanation: P1 runs 0-5 and P2 runs 5-8, so P3 starts at 8. Waiting time = start time minus arrival time = 8 - 2 = 6 ms.

questions.concept: PostgreSQL network address data types
questions.question: PostgreSQL provides built-in data types to store which kind of values?
questions.explanation: PostgreSQL supports data types to store IPv4, IPv6 and MAC addresses.

questions.concept: Constant time algorithm complexity
questions.question: An algorithm whose running time does not depend on the size of the input is said to have a time complexity of:
questions.explanation: A constant time algorithm has time complexity 1; linear is n and quadratic is n^2.

questions.concept: Sequence of the six SDLC stages
questions.question: Which sequence correctly lists the six SDLC stages?

options.A: Planning, Requirement Analysis, Development, Design, Deployment, Maintenance
options.B: Planning, Requirement Analysis, Design, Development, Deployment, Maintenance
options.C: Planning, Design, Requirement Analysis, Development, Maintenance, Deployment
options.D: Requirement Analysis, Planning, Design, Development, Deployment, Maintenance

questions.explanation: The stages are Planning, Requirement Analysis, Design, Development, Deployment and Maintenance in that order.

questions.concept: Gyroscope tracks rotation of the hand
questions.question: In a smartphone game, the player twists their hand to steer. Which sensor tracks this rotation or twist?
questions.explanation: A gyroscope tracks the rotation or twist of the hand, while the accelerometer detects orientation of the phone.

questions.concept: EDI definition
questions.question: Direct computer-to-computer transfer of transaction information contained in standard business documents is called:
questions.explanation: EDI is the direct computer-to-computer exchange of standard business documents; EFT and ECS move money, and SCM is a chain of partners.

questions.concept: Network octets in a Class C address
questions.question: For the address 200.1.1.5 with its default mask, how many octets form the network portion?
questions.explanation: 200 is Class C (192-223), format N.N.N.H, so three octets are network and one is host.

questions.concept: Fake emails and websites as spoofing
questions.question: Sending fake emails or setting up fake websites that pretend to come from a trusted source is an example of:
questions.explanation: Spoofing covers fake emails, phone calls, websites and IP spoofing.

questions.concept: IMAP for server-side mail management
questions.question: A user wants to view and organise e-mails on the server without downloading them, synchronised across several devices. Which protocol suits this?
questions.explanation: IMAP manipulates mail on the server with synchronization; POP3 downloads mail and SMTP sends outgoing mail.

questions.concept: System analysis as detailed study of existing system
questions.question: The detailed study of the existing system, carried out to understand how it works and where it falls short, is called:
questions.explanation: A detailed study of the existing system is termed system analysis; design, testing and deployment come later in the life cycle.

questions.concept: XOR used in error detection and encryption
questions.question: Which logic gate is commonly used in arithmetic operations, error detection and encryption?
questions.explanation: XOR is used in arithmetic, error detection, encryption and data selection; XNOR in data synchronization and multiplexing.

questions.concept: Roles of * and & in pointer declaration
questions.question: In the C++ statement int *p = &x; the symbols * and & respectively:

options.A: Return the address of x, and declare p as a pointer
options.B: Declare p as a pointer, and return the address of x
options.C: Multiply p by x, and perform bitwise AND
options.D: Dereference x, and allocate memory dynamically

questions.explanation: In a declaration * marks p as a pointer, and & is the address-of operator returning the memory address of x.

questions.concept: SQL is non-procedural, specifies what not how
questions.question: Which statement best describes how an SQL query specifies the data to be retrieved?

options.A: It states step by step how the data is to be fetched
options.B: It must name the storage file and disk block to read
options.C: It must give a loop that visits each row in order
options.D: It states what data to retrieve, not how to retrieve it

questions.explanation: SQL does not require specifying how to get the data; the user only specifies what to retrieve and the DBMS works out the method.

questions.concept: Java developer and companies
questions.question: Java was developed by James Gosling at ____ and later acquired by ____.
questions.explanation: Java was developed at Sun Microsystems by James Gosling; Sun was later acquired by Oracle Corporation.

questions.concept: Counting strings of a* up to length 2
questions.question: Over the alphabet {a}, how many strings of length at most 2 are generated by the regular expression a*?
questions.explanation: Kleene star means zero or more repetitions, giving the empty string, a and aa: 3 strings (a+ would give only 2).

questions.concept: SIMM pins and voltage
questions.question: Which memory module comes in 30-pin and 72-pin versions, stores 4 MB to 64 MB and works at 5 volts?
questions.explanation: SIMM has 30/72 pins, 4-64 MB and 5 V; DIMM has 168/184/240 pins, 32 MB-1 GB and 3.3 V.

questions.concept: readlines() returns a list of lines
questions.question: What does readlines() return when called on a file object opened for reading?

options.A: Only the first line of the file
options.B: A list of strings, one for each line, each ending with a newline character
options.C: One string containing the whole file
options.D: A tuple containing the number of lines and characters

questions.explanation: readlines() reads all lines and returns them as a list of strings. read() returns the whole file as one string, and readline() returns one line.

questions.concept: Internal fragmentation in fixed partitions
questions.question: Memory uses fixed partitions of 50 KB each. Processes of 40 KB, 45 KB and 30 KB are each placed in a separate partition. What is the total internal fragmentation?
questions.explanation: Wasted space inside partitions is (50 - 40) + (50 - 45) + (50 - 30) = 10 + 5 + 20 = 35 KB.

questions.concept: Multiple updates through a reassigned pointer
questions.explanation: *p += b changes a to 30. Then p points to b and *p = *p * 2 changes b to 40, leaving a at 30.

questions.concept: Pumping lemma as an important TOC concept
questions.question: Which of the following is listed as an important concept in Theory of Computation?
questions.explanation: The pumping lemma is listed with finite automata, regular expressions, CFGs, Turing machines, decidability and the halting problem.
